Name: Praveen Kamath
Question: When did you feel like a complete savage?
Answer: I had visited my home town a month back to attend my cousin's wedding. On the sangeet day, I interacted with many old relatives. And I swear most conversations ended with Beta shaadi kab karoge? (when are you marrying?) Some sarcasms weren't even essential. Me: Hi aunty. How are you? Aunty: Doing fine. You are next in the line for marriage (winks at me). Another one. Me: Hey aunty. Should I get you a lemonade? Aunty: Sure. I don't think you will get time to serve us once you are married. So better serve us now. I got furious. Decided to sit alone for a while away from my relatives. When suddenly I hear some conversation going on besides me. Some aunty: He is XYZ's grandson. He is 26, single and stays in Mumbai. Better we talk to his parents about marriage. The next day (cousin’s marriage), one of the above aunties advised me to marry soon as this is the right age. Aunty: Son, you should marry soon. This is the right age. Me: Hold on. Let me talk to my girl-friend about this right now. I left the seat and pretended to call someone . I didn't see her when I came back. I saw her during lunch. I stood next to her and I said 'Aunty. She said next month would be fine. Do come. '. She went away without uttering a word! **thug life music playing in my head** Now that aunty is a classic orthodox who is against love marriages. Thus this was my savage moment. P.S: I don't think I am going to get any marriage proposals post this incident.

Question: Why did the Tesla Cybertruck's window break?
Answer: It’s a genius marketing move known as Guerrilla marketing (as pointed out by Samuel Bracke). Create some content for people to talk about, let them make a fuss of it on social networking platforms. Voila! They just promoted your product. Moreover, a vehicles side window glass should be shatterproof, not unbreakable. Imagine you crashed your car and the doors are jammed. Breaking the glass with a tool is your only escape route. If you come across 2 advertisement hoardings, one which is perfect and the other one with typos, which one will catch your attention and which one will last longer in your memories? Obviously the one with mistakes. People don’t remember the good, just the bad. Image source: Google

Question: If a restaurant customer drops their food on the floor accidentally (like a whole burger), should the restaurant replace it or should the customer?
Answer: A girl walks into McDonalds. Her friends gather around and give her hugs. It’s her birthday. She moves towards the counter to place her order, me standing behind her to place mine. She orders around 8–10 meals. Takes out her card and hands it over to the cashier. The transactions fails. She, worried, checks her bank balance. She tells the cashier to swipe Rs. 1500 and pays the remaining Rs. 200 by cash. The order arrives. Her friend takes the tray with burgers and fries. She takes the one with 8–10 cups of coke. She trips over a table and drops the tray. :( The janitor immediately starts cleaning the floor. She panics, moves towards the cashier, stopped for a second, then starts walking towards her table. Her friends tell her it’s OK. She wanted to buy the coke but maybe that’s all the money she had. A waiter arrives at her table with a tray of cokes. She blooms with happiness. Upon asking the waiter weather she bought the coke again, the waiter replied ‘No sir. This one was on the house. No one should be sad on their birthday.’ So, it depends on the restaurant, the people working their and the occasion.
